welcome.title: Welcome, Explorer!
welcome.pari_tip: There are no wrong ideas in this workbook. Try your best, ask questions, and have fun learning about AI!

syllabus.objective: I can give examples of AI in different fields.
I can organise data, draw a bar graph and spot unclean data.
I can explain the machine learning steps and work out
I can explain how computers see pictures as pixels.
I can write clear prompts and check AI answers.
I can judge if an AI is fair and responsible.
I can check if information is real before I share it.
I can use design thinking to plan a solution.

units.title: AI in Our World
learn_paragraphs:
AI is used in many fields. In health it helps doctors read scans. In farming
it spots sick leaves from photos.
In transport it finds the fastest route. In language it translates speech. In
shopping it gives recommendations.
AI is a tool. People decide how to use it, and people stay responsible.

new_words.definition: how often the AI is right
a use of technology for a job
a machine doing a task by itself

units.did_you_know: Translation apps can translate between many Indian languages, like Hindi, Marathi and Tamil.
units.think_and_talk: Which job do you think AI should never do alone? Why?
units.self_check: I can give examples of AI in different fields.

units.title: Data and Charts
learn_paragraphs:
Data is useful when it is organised in a dataset, like a table.
A bar graph shows data as bars, so patterns are easy to see.
AI needs clean data: correct, complete and with no copies. Wrong data
teaches wrong answers.

new_words.definition: a chart that uses bars to show amounts
data that is correct and complete
a collection of organised data

units.did_you_know: Big AI models learn from huge datasets, far more text than one person could read in a lifetime.
units.think_and_talk: How could wrong data make an AI give a wrong answer?
units.self_check: I can organise data, draw a bar graph and spot unclean data.

units.title: How Machines Learn
learn_paragraphs:
Machine learning has steps: collect data → label it → train → test →
improve.
A trained AI is called a model.
We measure a model with accuracy: correct answers out of the total. 18
right out of 20 is 90% accuracy.

new_words.definition: a fake video or voice made with AI
understanding how others feel
treating everyone equally

units.did_you_know: Engineers keep some data aside just for testing, so the AI is checked on examples it has never seen.
units.think_and_talk: Is 100% accuracy on training pictures enough? Why not?

units.title: Computer Vision
learn_paragraphs:
Computers see pictures as tiny squares called pixels. Each pixel is stored as
numbers for its colour.
AI looks for features: edges, shapes, colours and textures.
This is how phones unlock with faces and apps read text from photos.

new_words.definition: a detail that helps recognise something
to come up with many ideas
a picture stored as data

units.did_you_know: A phone photo can have more than 10 million pixels.
units.think_and_talk: Why might AI find it hard to recognise things in the dark?
units.self_check: I can explain how computers see pictures as pixels.

units.title: Language AI and Prompts
learn_paragraphs:
AI chatbots learn from lots of text and predict the next word, again and
again, to write a response.
A prompt is what we ask. A good prompt has a task, details and a format.
Chatbots can make mistakes. Check facts, and never share private
information.

new_words.definition: when computers learn from data
a trained AI
one tiny square in a picture

units.did_you_know: AI chatbots build their answers one small piece of a word at a time.
units.think_and_talk: Why might two people get different answers from the same chatbot?
units.self_check: I can write clear prompts and check AI answers.

units.title: Fair and Responsible AI
learn_paragraphs:
Responsible AI is fair to everyone, safe, honest about being AI and
protects privacy.
If data leaves out some people, the AI may not work well for them.
Humans must stay in charge and fix problems. That is being responsible.

new_words.definition: to guess what comes next
keeping personal information safe
the question or instruction we give AI

units.did_you_know: Many countries are making rules to keep AI safe and fair.
units.think_and_talk: Who should fix an AI that is unfair: the users, the makers, or both?
units.self_check: I can judge if an AI is fair and responsible.

units.title: Fact or Fake?
learn_paragraphs:
AI can make pictures, voices and videos that look real. A fake video of a
real person is called a deepfake.
Before you believe or share, verify: Who made it? Is the source trusted?
Do other trusted sources say the same?
Use STOP: Source, Think, Other sources, Pause before sharing.

new_words.definition: a first simple model of an idea
a suggestion made for you
the answer AI gives

units.did_you_know: Fake pictures sometimes have clues, like odd hands, strange shadows or blurry writing.
units.think_and_talk: What would you do if a friend shared a video that looked fake?
units.self_check: I can check if information is real before I share it.

lines: “Robot elected class monitor in a Delhi school!”
Source: Who made this? Is it a trusted website?
Think: Does it sound possible or too strange?
Other sources: Do other trusted sources say the same?
Pause: Should I share it? Why or why not?
If it is on the internet, it must be true.
Checking 2 trusted sources is a good habit.
It is fine to share a surprising video before checking.

units.title: Design Thinking
learn_paragraphs:
Innovators solve problems with design thinking: Empathise → Define →
Ideate → Prototype → Test.
Empathy means understanding how others feel. Start by listening to the
people with the problem.
A prototype is a first, simple model, like a paper sketch of an app.

new_words.definition: taking care of what you make and do
where information comes from
to check if something is true

units.did_you_know: Many famous apps started as sketches on paper!
units.think_and_talk: Why is it important to talk to the people who have the problem?
units.self_check: I can use design thinking to plan a solution.
